newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somali faction says it will free Australian pilot.
newsitem.headline: Somali faction says it will free Australian pilot.

text.p: The Somali faction led by Hussein Aideed said on Friday it would free within three days an Australian pilot jailed for 25 years for making a forced landing in Somalia.
Hussein Abdulle Alasow, minister of justice in a government led by Aideed, said Justin Fraser, 25, would be released to an international organisation working in south Mogadishu or to his relatives.

He said Aideed, elected president of Somalia by supporters last month after the death of his father, accepted a request for Fraser's release from Dominic Langenbacher, the U.N. Development Programme resident and humanitarian coordinator for Somalia.
Langenbacher visited Aideed in Mogadishu on September 1.
Fraser was forced to land at an airstrip in May in the western Somali town of Huddur held by Aideed's militia when the plane he was flying from Kenya developed engine trouble.
He was charged with violating the Aideed faction's airspace and put on trial in the southwestern town of Baidoa, found guilty and sentenced to 25 years in jail and a fine of $485,000.

Hussein Aideed, who wants international aid organisations to return to areas under his control, said on August 7 he would review Fraser's case. Hussein Aideed, a 34-year-old former U.S. marine, succeeded his 62-year-old father shortly after his death on August 1.
Officials said Fraser was jailed in the southwestern town of Baidoa, which Mohamed Farah Aideed's forces seized a year ago. Australia said in June Fraser was seriously sick.
Fraser's plane was loaded with qat, the leaves and bark of a bush which when chewed act as a mild stimulant. It is flown in daily as part of a multi-million dollar business from Kenya and Ethiopia.

All international aid agencies withdrew foreign staff from south Mogadishu and other areas controlled by the Aideed faction earlier this year because of insecurity and repeated bids to force them and donors to recognise the government.
Somalia has had no central government or authority since the overthrow of late dictator Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
